Meeting header: 2026-03-04 16:00 UTC | Duration: 42 mins | Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Sam (Triton CTO), Leah (ML Eng), Jordan (Infra)

[00:00] Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, on the calendar this is a discovery for Triton's migration off OpenAI to either Redwood Dedicated or Private. I'm Alex, AE on the account, with Priya from our solutions team. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Sam (Triton): Doing good, thanks. Ready to dive in.
[00:12] Leah (Triton): Yep, thanks Alex. We had a quick agenda in the invite — stack, constraints, and then technical questions.
[00:20] Priya (Redwood): Sounds great. Quick housekeeping — we'll take notes, share resources, and plan a tech deep dive after this if that works.
[00:27] Jordan (Triton): Works for us. We're mainly evaluating cost and latency, plus compliance — we have SOC2 and some EU data residency needs.
[00:35] Alex (Redwood): Perfect. Can you give us a quick overview of your current setup and pain points?
[00:40] Sam (Triton): Sure. We use OpenAI for chat generation and embeddings. ~200M tokens/month today, spikes to 500M during launches. Latency is sometimes okay but unpredictable; cost is creeping up. We also have an internal preference to host on dedicated infra for predictable throughput and better controls.
[00:55] Leah (Triton): Also, we're running some experimental local inference with vLM — I mean vLLM — and T G I variants for cost testing, but those aren't stable in prod yet. The trouble is eval parity: outputs differ a bit across vLLM/TGI/OpenAI and we worry about regressions if we switch runtimes.
[01:12] Priya (Redwood): Totally understandable. A couple things we usually look at: model parity (same model family/weights), tokenization and sampling settings, and runtime differences like kv cache handling and attention kernel precision. Those can cause slight output shifts.
[01:28] Sam (Triton): Right. Can Redwood guarantee API compatibility with OpenAI's completions and chat endpoints? We have hundreds of microservices calling OpenAI directly.
[01:35] Alex (Redwood): Short answer: high compatibility. Our Hosted API aims for drops-in replacements for most OpenAI flows, and Dedicated can be configured to accept the same request shapes. There are edge cases — function calling and some newer SDK behaviors — where we might need tiny client-side changes.
[01:50] Leah (Triton): What about eval parity then? If we move to Dedicated or Private, what's the recommended approach to ensure outputs match our golden eval sets?
[01:57] Priya (Redwood): We recommend a two-phase approach: 1) match model variant and sampling params, 2) run a shadow eval on a small prompt set to compare distributions — we provide tooling to run these comparisons and surface drift metrics. If a parity gap appears, we can tune quantization, or suggest a different model variant.
[02:16] Jordan (Triton): You mentioned quantization — we're already experimenting with 4-bit and 8-bit for cost. How does that affect quality?
[02:22] Priya (Redwood): Quantization can introduce small artifacts. Our Optimize tooling has profiles by workload; for many chat workloads, 4-bit quantization with per-channel scales can keep regression under thresholds, but it depends on the model. We can run a targeted eval to measure delta in Rouge/BLEU or your custom metrics.
[02:38] Sam (Triton): On runtime: we run vLLM for batching today for internal tests. How does Redwood's runtime compare for throughput and latency?
[02:45] Priya (Redwood): Our runtime is GPU-optimized with continuous batching, KV cache management, and optimized kernels. In many cases we see better tail latency than stock vLLM because of kernel selection and batching heuristics, but it depends on sequence length distribution and hardware. We have benchmarks we can share.
[02:59] Alex (Redwood): I'll attach the benchmark spreadsheet and per-model performance profiles after the call.
[03:05] Leah (Triton): Great. On networking and security: for Dedicated or Private we need VPC peering, customer-managed KMS, and audit logs. Can we get SSO and RBAC?
[03:13] Alex (Redwood): Yes — Dedicated supports VPC peering, Private adds on-prem options, and both support customer KMS/HSM, SAML SSO, role-based access controls, and audit trails. Priya will share the SOC2/ISO docs and the security whitepaper.
[03:26] Jordan (Triton): Are there specific latency SLOs for Dedicated? We need predictable p95 under 200ms for short prompts.
[03:33] Priya (Redwood): With Dedicated and appropriate GPU sizing and batch configs we can hit a p95 around 150-180ms for shorter prompts on A100-like hardware; for long context it's different. We can size a reserved pool to meet your SLOs.
[03:47] Sam (Triton): What's the migration path for our services? We have many microservices calling OpenAI — do you support a proxy or SDK shim?
[03:55] Alex (Redwood): We offer an API gateway and client SDKs that mimic OpenAI request shapes. Many customers do a phased cutover: redirect a percentage of traffic to Redwood Hosted for validation, then Dedicated. We also support canary rollouts and automatic fallback to the upstream provider during the transition.
[04:14] Leah (Triton): About costs — can you give us a ballpark comparison? We're paying X per token with OpenAI and running experiments with TGI to reduce cost.
[04:22] Alex (Redwood): Ballpark is tricky without knowing your traffic profile and model choices. Dedicated is typically lower unit cost at commit, but requires reserved capacity. Hosted is easier to start. We'll send a pricing grid showing delta vs OpenAI and expected ROI for a migration.
[04:36] Jordan (Triton): Will Dedicated require us to manage deployments or do you handle scaling?
[04:41] Priya (Redwood): We manage the control plane and can operate the runtime; Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and autoscaling policies. You get observability and we'll work with your infra team on network setup.
[04:53] Sam (Triton): One technical thing — our eval shows that OpenAI 'gpt-...' model outputs are slightly different than the same open weights running on vLLM. How much of that is tokenizer or sampling differences vs backend optimizations?
[05:02] Priya (Redwood): It can be all of the above. Tokenizer differences can create offsets, sampling RNG seeds differ, and runtime implementations (attention kernels, numeric precision) change outputs. We usually start by harmonizing tokenization and seed, then look at precision/quantization and sampling code paths.
[05:21] Leah (Triton): Do you support function-calling semantics similar to OpenAI's function call? We rely on that heavily.
[05:27] Alex (Redwood): Yes, we support function/tool calling patterns and structured outputs. There are small differences in metadata fields in some SDKs; we'll document those and help with a compatibility layer.
[05:39] Jordan (Triton): For the private on-prem option, do you support air-gapped installs and local KMS?
[05:45] Priya (Redwood): Yes, our Private deployment is designed for regulated customers. We have an air-gapped package and integrations for customer-managed KMS/HSM. We'll need to understand your ops constraints to size the install.
[05:57] Sam (Triton): Great. Can Redwood run a benchmark with our prompt set? We'd like side-by-side with OpenAI and TGI/vLLM.
[06:04] Priya (Redwood): Absolutely. If you share the prompt set and traffic profile we'll schedule a bench run. We can run it on Hosted first for parity, then on Dedicated or Private for perf numbers.
[06:16] Alex (Redwood): For the bench we typically ask for: representative prompt set, concurrency profile, desired latency SLOs, and your evaluation metrics.
[06:25] Leah (Triton): We'll grab a 1k prompt sample from our evals and annotate the key success metrics.
[06:30] Sam (Triton): On legal/comms — contract, data retention, and indemnity are important. Who owns logs and PII?
[06:36] Alex (Redwood): With Dedicated your data is isolated; retention policies and audit logs are configurable. We can engage Legal after the tech deep-dive to align on contract terms.
[06:46] Jordan (Triton): Any limits on model support? We're evaluating some open models not in your catalog.
[06:51] Priya (Redwood): We onboard a wide range of open models and can bring custom weights. There are compute considerations for very large models; we'll evaluate feasibility.
[07:00] Sam (Triton): How do you handle fallback policies if capacity is constrained? For launches we sometimes need bursting.
[07:06] Alex (Redwood): We support burst capacity and smart routing — you can define fallback to Hosted or another region/model variant automatically.
[07:15] Leah (Triton): A couple clarifying questions on logs — is PII redacted automatically or do we need to handle that?
[07:21] Priya (Redwood): We provide both raw and redacted logs; redaction can be enabled and tailored to your rules. For compliance you'd likely want redaction plus audit trails.
[07:34] Sam (Triton): Excellent. Anything else we should flag?
[07:37] Alex (Redwood): One more: rollout strategy. We recommend a canary with 5-10% traffic, run golden evals, then ramp. We'll help with tooling for comparison.
[07:47] Leah (Triton): Sounds good. Let's talk timelines — Triton is aiming to decide by end of Q2 and start a pilot in July.
[07:55] Alex (Redwood): That timeline works. We'll prioritize benchmark availability and make sure security signoffs are in the same cadence.
[08:02] Priya (Redwood): I'll coordinate with you on SOC2 docs and set up a slot for a 2-hour technical deep-dive where we can do a live bench.
[08:11] Sam (Triton): Perfect.
[08:13] Alex (Redwood): Quick recap and next steps — I'll send pricing and the benchmark spreadsheet; Priya will share security docs and propose deep-dive times; Sam/Leah/Jordan will share the prompt set and traffic profile. Anything to add?
[08:26] Jordan (Triton): No, that's it.
[08:28] Leah (Triton): Thanks all.
[08:30] Alex (Redwood): Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the items.

Notes on transcript quality: Auto-transcription had minor errors (vLM -> vLLM, T G I tokenization). Shared artifacts referenced during call: link to benchmarking spreadsheet (sent after call), security whitepaper (to be sent).
